title: 3 Days in Seoul: a first-timer's plan

slides.title: Here's a 3-day plan
slides.voice: First time in Seoul? Here's a three-day plan that won't wear you out.

slides.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace
slides.voice: Day one. Gyeongbokgung Palace, early, before the crowds. It's closed on Tuesdays.

slides.title: Bukchon's hanok lanes
slides.sub: People live here: keep it quiet
slides.voice: Then the hanok lanes of Bukchon. People live here, so keep it quiet.

slides.title: Cheonggyecheon at night
slides.sub: A free, easy walk, lit up after dark
slides.voice: At night, walk along Cheonggyecheon stream. It's free, and lit up after dark.

slides.title: Gwangjang Market
slides.sub: Try bindaetteok, a mung bean pancake
slides.voice: Day two. Eat at Gwangjang Market. Try bindaetteok, a crispy mung bean pancake.

slides.title: Shop in Myeongdong
slides.sub: Bring your passport for tax refunds
slides.voice: Shop in Myeongdong, and bring your passport for tax refunds.

slides.title: Namsan and N Seoul Tower
slides.sub: The best free view of the city
slides.voice: Then watch the sunset from Namsan.

slides.title: Choose your own Seoul
slides.sub: Secret Garden, Han River or a jjimjilbang
slides.voice: Day three is yours. The Secret Garden at Changdeokgung, a Han River park, or a Korean bathhouse.

slides.title: Full plan and tips
slides.voice: The full plan is on Korea Plainly. Link in bio.
